"I need you to take over part of the coordination with Helena for the next few weeks."

Daniel frowned.

"Is there a problem with her?"

"No."

"With the project?"

"Not that either."

"Then why?"

Alexander looked at him.

"Because I need you there."

Daniel held his gaze for a few seconds.

"Does this have something to do with the two of you?"

Alexander remained silent.

Daniel slowly exhaled.

"I don't want to get involved."

"I'm not asking you to."

"It sounds like you are."

"I'm asking you to do your job."

Daniel nodded.

"All right."

When he left, Alexander looked at the door again.

He knew he was making everything worse.

But he had no other choice.

That afternoon, Helena noticed that Daniel had received new responsibilities within the project. She did not ask why. She simply accepted it. Perhaps it was even better. Having Daniel around made the meetings easier and, above all, kept her from having to be alone with Alexander.

Over the following days, the change became obvious.

Alexander began traveling more frequently.

Meetings were transferred to other directors.

Some documents that had previously gone directly through him began being forwarded to Claire.

And although Helena could not explain exactly why, she felt that something was happening inside Blackwood.

It was not just Alexander.

It was the entire family.

She noticed it for the first time during a meeting when one of the directors entered the room, spoke quickly with Claire, and left without even looking at the others. Shortly afterward, Claire closed her laptop and announced that the presentation would be postponed.

"Why?" Helena asked.

Claire hesitated.

"Internal matters."

"Does it affect the project?"

"Not yet."

Yet.

The word remained in Helena's mind.

That night, when she left the office, she found Daniel waiting in the lobby.

"Are you going straight home?"

"Yes."

"Can I ask you something?"

Helena smiled faintly.

"Depends."

"Do you know what's going on?"

She frowned.

"With the project?"

"With Blackwood."

Helena fell silent.

"No."

Daniel put his hands in his pockets.

"I don't either."

"Why did you ask?"

"Because Alexander is different."

Helena looked away.

"He's been different for a while."

"More than before."

She did not answer.

Daniel watched her for a few seconds.

"You don't have to tell me anything."

"There's nothing to tell."

"All right."

He paused.

"Just be careful."

Helena looked up.

"Careful of what?"

Daniel took a moment before answering.

"I don't know."

And that was precisely the part that bothered her most.

Because, for the first time, someone had said aloud the feeling she had been trying to ignore.

Something was wrong.

While Helena headed home, Alexander was somewhere else in the city, sitting in a private hospital room.

His father was awake.

Pale, tired, and much more fragile than Alexander allowed himself to admit, Richard Blackwood looked at his son when he entered.

"Did you tell her?"

Alexander stopped.

"No."

"About me?"

"No."

"About the company?"

"That too."

Richard breathed with difficulty.

"Then she still doesn't know."

"No."

"And you intend to keep her away?"

Alexander approached the bed.

"As long as I can."

His father watched him in silence.

"She's important to you."

Alexander did not answer.

Richard smiled faintly.

"You don't have to say it."

"I'm not doing this for myself."

"That's exactly why you're doing it."

Alexander looked away.

"You don't understand."

"I understand more than you think."

Richard paused before continuing.

"When I started building all of this, I thought protecting my family meant controlling everything around them. It took me many years to realize it doesn't work that way."

Alexander remained silent.

"What happened to your mother cannot happen again."

The sentence made Alexander look up.

"Don't talk about her."

"You need to know."

"Not now."

"Especially now."

Richard took a deep breath.

"What is happening did not begin with you. Or with your brother. It began long before."

Alexander felt tension move through his body.

"What are you saying?"

His father looked toward the door before looking back at him.

"There are things about the Blackwoods that you still don't know."

Alexander remained still.

"What things?"

Richard did not answer immediately.

"When I can, I'll tell you everything."

"Dad..."

"Not yet."

"You can't keep saying that."

"I can."

His voice was weak but firm.

"Because if I tell you now, you'll make a decision without having all the information."

Alexander moved closer.

"Then give me the information."

Richard closed his eyes for a moment.

"Don't trust anyone who is trying to rush your succession."

Alexander felt a chill run down his spine.

"Who is trying?"

His father opened his eyes.

"That's what you need to find out."

Before Alexander could ask anything else, the door opened and a nurse entered to check the monitors.

The conversation ended.

But the words remained.

Don't trust anyone.

Alexander left the room a few minutes later and walked down the hospital corridor without realizing exactly where he was going. He stopped in front of a window and stared at the distant city while the pieces began to fit together in a way he did not like.

His father's illness.

The succession.

The leaked documents.

The information about the project.

The person inside the family.

And Helena.

Everything seemed connected.

His phone vibrated in his pocket.

A message.

Alexander opened it.

It was a photograph.

Helena leaving the Blackwood building that afternoon.

He stood still.

Beneath the photograph was a single sentence:

"You should have kept her away."

Alexander's heart raced.

He looked both ways down the corridor.

No one.

He opened the image again.

There was no doubt.

Someone was watching Helena.

Someone knew that she was important to him.

And for the first time since everything had begun, Alexander realized that it might already be too late to keep her out of the story.

The following morning, Helena arrived at the office as usual.

But before she even entered the elevator, she received a message from an unknown number.

"We need to talk about Alexander Blackwood."

She stared at the screen.

For a few seconds, she considered deleting the message.

She didn't.

Because after weeks of trying to understand why Alexander had changed, why his family seemed to be involved in some dispute no one would explain, and why everyone seemed to be hiding something, that message awakened a certainty she could no longer ignore.

Perhaps the kiss had never been the real secret.

Perhaps it had only been the first thing she had discovered by accident.

And for the first time, Helena had the feeling that the distance Alexander had created between them was not merely a form of rejection.

It was a desperate attempt to keep her away from something she still could not see.

She locked the screen of her phone.

The elevator doors opened.

Helena stepped inside.

This time, however, she was not thinking about work.

She was thinking about the Blackwoods.

And the message she had just received.

Because if someone was willing to contact her to talk about Alexander, perhaps the secret he had been trying to protect no longer belonged only to him.

chapters.title: The First Truth
chapters.content:
The morning after the message, Helena woke before her alarm and spent several minutes staring at the ceiling, trying to decide whether she should simply ignore it. Her phone was on the bedside table, its screen dark, but she could still remember every word she had read the night before. “We need to talk about Alexander Blackwood.” There was no name, no familiar number, and no explanation of who had sent it. It was too short to be considered a threat and too specific to be dismissed as something casual. Helena had reread the sentence several times, looking for some detail that might reveal the sender's identity, but she had found nothing. It could have been someone from the company, someone connected to the Blackwood family, or even someone who knew just enough to try to frighten her. The problem was that, after everything that had happened, she could no longer consider any of those possibilities absurd.

She got up, showered, and dressed for work as she did every morning, but her routine seemed to have acquired a different layer of tension. While making coffee, she thought about Alexander. She thought about the kiss, the way he had acted the following day, the distance that had settled between them, and, above all, the persistent feeling that something did not make sense. For weeks, she had tried to believe that Alexander had simply regretted what happened. It was a painful explanation, but an understandable one. People could act on impulse, make decisions they later wished to forget, and retreat when they realized the consequences. What she could not explain was why, at the same time Alexander was pushing her away, he seemed increasingly concerned with everything happening around him. Meetings were being canceled, conversations stopped when she entered a room, schedules changed suddenly, and there was a tension that had not existed when they first began working together. Now there was also an anonymous message.

Perhaps it was time to stop accepting that it was not her problem.

Helena picked up her phone and opened the conversation again. The number was still unknown. For a few seconds, she kept her thumb over the reply field, unsure what exactly to write. She could ask who the person was. She could demand an explanation. She could simply block the number and pretend it had never happened. None of the three options seemed satisfactory. If the person really had information about Alexander, ignoring them could mean losing an opportunity to discover what was happening. If it was merely an attempt at provocation, replying might be exactly what they expected.

After hesitating for a few more seconds, Helena typed only:

“Who are you?”

She sent it.

The response came almost immediately.

“Someone who knows you shouldn't trust him.”

Helena felt her stomach tighten.

She typed again.

“Trust whom?”

The response took longer.

“Alexander.”

She closed her eyes for a moment.

That was the part that bothered her most. There was nothing new about that statement. Ever since she had met Alexander, trusting him had never been simple. He hid information, controlled conversations, made decisions without explaining his reasons, and seemed to believe he could carry everything happening around him on his own. Helena had already learned to live with that professionally. What made the message different was the possibility that someone outside the situation was observing exactly the same things she had begun to notice.

“What do you know about him?” she wrote.

This time, the response did not come immediately.

Helena waited.

One minute.

Two.

Five.

Nothing.

She put the phone in her bag, but she could not shake the feeling that she had just opened a door she might never be able to close again.

On the way to the office, she tried to think rationally. She should not draw conclusions based on anonymous messages. She should not assume that Alexander was hiding something related to the project simply because certain things seemed strange. And, above all, she should not allow a stranger to determine how she saw someone she had been working with for months. Still, when she entered the Blackwood building, she immediately noticed that something was different.

Two men she had never seen before were speaking quietly near the reception desk.

One of the female directors came out of an elevator accompanied by a lawyer.

And when Helena approached the desk, the receptionist looked up and smiled, but her smile seemed to disappear quickly when she realized who it was.

“Good morning, Helena.”

“Good morning.”

“Are you going to the project floor?”

“Yes.”

The woman hesitated.

“Mr. Blackwood has already arrived.”

Helena frowned slightly.

“All right.”

There was no reason for that information to sound strange. Alexander almost always arrived before her. Still, something in the way the receptionist had said it made Helena pay closer attention.

“Did something happen?”

“Not that I know of.”

The answer came too quickly.

Helena simply nodded.

“Thank you.”

She entered the elevator and pressed the button for the floor. When the doors closed, she took her phone out of her bag again. No new message.

She put it away and took a deep breath.

She would not look for Alexander immediately.

First, she would observe.

Perhaps that was what she should have done from the beginning.

When she reached the project floor, she found Daniel leaving a room with several documents in his hands. He stopped when he saw her.

“Good morning.”

“Good morning.”

Daniel studied her face for a few seconds.

“Are you all right?”

Helena smiled faintly.

“I am.”

“That answer sounds familiar.”

She looked at him.

“Familiar?”

“You always answer like that when you're clearly thinking about something.”

Helena let out a small laugh.

“Maybe I'm just tired.”

“Then I'll believe you.”

Daniel lifted the documents.

“The meeting with the merchants was moved up to this morning.”

“I didn't know.”

“They changed it last night.”

“Who changed it?”

“Claire.”

Helena nodded.

“All right.”

Daniel began walking beside her.

“They also canceled the afternoon meeting with the finance team.”

“Again?”

“Again.”

Helena fell silent.

Daniel noticed.

“It's starting to get strange.”

“What?”

“All of this.”

She looked at him.

“You noticed it too?”

“It's hard not to. For two weeks, no one explains anything. Some meetings disappear from the calendar, others appear at the last minute, and everyone seems to know something I don't.”

Helena tightened her grip on her bag.

“Maybe they're just internal matters.”

Daniel shrugged.

“Maybe.”

They reached the meeting room, where Claire was already waiting. Three other people were seated at the table, but Alexander was not among them.

Helena felt a small pang of disappointment that she immediately tried to ignore.

Claire opened the meeting with several updates about the project, but most of them concerned decisions that had been postponed. The schedule officially remained unchanged, although no one seemed able to explain why so many stages were being reviewed. When Helena asked about the approval of one of the intervention proposals, Claire replied that the board still needed to analyze a few points.

“Which points?” Helena asked.

Claire closed the folder.

“Internal matters.”

“Related to the project?”

“In part.”

Helena waited for an explanation that never came.

“Could this affect the deadline?”

Claire glanced quickly at Daniel before answering.

“We don't know yet.”

It was the third time in less than ten minutes that someone had used a vague answer to an objective question.

Helena leaned back in her chair.

Something was happening.

And for the first time, she was certain it was not just her imagination.

After the meeting, Daniel waited until the others had left.

“You're thinking what I'm thinking too?”

Helena picked up some documents.

“Depends.”

“That something is wrong.”

She looked at him.

“I think there's something they're not telling the team.”

Daniel put his hands in his pockets.

“I don't know if that's our problem.”

“Maybe it isn't yet.”

“And you're worried?”

Helena hesitated.

“A little.”

Daniel watched her carefully.

“If you find out something, be careful.”

“Careful about what?”

“About whom you ask.”

The sentence hung between them for several seconds.

Helena smiled without humor.

“You're starting to sound mysterious.”

“I'm not trying to.”

“You're succeeding.”

Daniel sighed.

“I just know that when people start hiding information inside a company this large, there's usually a reason.”

Helena did not answer.

She thought about the message.

She thought about Alexander.

And for the first time, she realized that Daniel was right about one thing: perhaps the problem was not discovering what was happening, but discovering whom she could trust while looking for the answer.

At the end of the morning, Alexander finally appeared in the meeting room. Helena was alone, reviewing some spreadsheets, when he entered. He stopped as soon as he saw her.

“Good morning.”

“Good morning.”

His gaze remained on her for a moment.

“Are you all right?”

The question immediately reminded Helena of the message.

“I am.”

Alexander approached.

“Are you sure?”

“Yes.”

He seemed to study her face.

“You're different.”

Helena closed the laptop.

“Maybe I'm tired.”

Alexander remained silent.

“Did something happen?”

She could have asked him directly about the leak. She could have shown him the message and demanded an explanation. For a moment, she considered doing exactly that. But something inside her told her to wait.

“No.”

Alexander continued looking at her.

“Helena...”

“We need to talk about the meeting with the merchants.”

He noticed the change of subject but did not insist.

“Of course.”

For the next few minutes, they discussed the project as if nothing had happened. Helena presented the numbers, Alexander made a few observations, and the two reached an agreement about the next steps. It was exactly the kind of conversation they had had dozens of times.

But now there was something beneath every word.

When they finished, Helena closed the folder.

“Alexander.”

He looked up.

“Yes?”

“Why are so many meetings being canceled?”

The question caught him off guard.

“What meetings?”

“Board, finance, some related to the project. Everything has changed in the past few weeks.”

Alexander was silent for a few seconds.

“There are some internal matters being resolved.”

“That is what Claire said.”

“Then she answered correctly.”

“And does it affect the project?”

“It might.”

Helena studied him.

“You knew about this when you asked me to attend the reception?”

Alexander's expression changed almost imperceptibly.

“Why are you asking that?”

“Because I want to understand.”

“Understand what?”

She took a deep breath.

“What is happening.”

Alexander moved closer to the table.

“Helena, some things don't need to involve you.”

Something inside her hardened at the words.

“That answer is starting to bother me.”

“I'm not trying to hide anything from you.”

“You are.”

He fell silent.

Helena stood.

“You've done this since we met. You decide what I need to know, what I don't, when I can participate in a conversation and when I should simply accept that there's an ‘internal matter.’ But now it's affecting my work.”

“I know.”

“Then tell me the truth.”

Alexander looked at her.

For a moment, she had the impression that he would finally do it.

But he didn't.

“Not yet.”

Helena felt her frustration rise.

“Then don't ask me to trust you.”

Alexander closed his eyes for a second.

“I'm not asking.”

“Maybe that's the problem.”

She picked up her bag and left.

Alexander remained alone in the room.

When the door closed, he placed both hands on the table and lowered his head. He did not want to lie to Helena. The problem was that the truth could put her in danger. Since the call he had received days earlier, he had increased security in certain areas of the building, restricted access to specific documents, and quietly asked that any information about the project be treated as confidential. Even so, someone was still leaking information.

And now someone was watching Helena.

He picked up his phone and opened the photograph he had received.

The image showed Helena leaving the Blackwood building.

It had been taken from a distance.

The time was visible.

The angle indicated that the person had probably been across the street.

Alexander had enlarged the photograph so many times that he already knew every detail of the frame. Helena's face was clear enough to leave no doubt.

This was not a generic threat.

It was a message.

Someone wanted him to know that she was being watched.

The phone rang.

It was his brother.

Alexander answered.

“Any news?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

“Our lawyer managed to access some of our father's old documents.”

Alexander fell silent.

“And?”

“The problem began before the last succession.”

“I already knew that.”

“No. You knew there were problems. You didn't know there were financial transactions connected to assets that don't appear in the current records.”

Alexander straightened.

“What kind of transactions?”

“Transfers to a company that shouldn't exist.”

“Who owns it?”

“We're still trying to find out.”

Alexander ran a hand over his face.

“And the project?”

“It appears in the documents.”

The silence stretched.

“How?”

“There are references to the properties in the historic district. Some were appraised years ago at values far below market.”

Alexander felt a weight in his chest.

“So someone knew the area would increase in value before we did.”

“Exactly.”

“And who had access to that information?”

“That is the question.”

Alexander looked again at Helena's photograph.

“We need to find out quickly.”

“I know.”

“And don't tell anyone about this.”

“Not even Claire?”

Alexander hesitated.

“Especially not until we're certain who is involved.”

The call ended a few minutes later.

Alexander remained seated, trying to organize the information. The revitalization was not merely an urban recovery project. Someone could be using information about the area to profit before property values increased. If that was true, the leaked documents were not part of an ordinary family dispute. Money was involved, and perhaps someone within the company's own structure had an interest in controlling the succession in order to continue accessing that information.

And Helena was in the middle of that project.

Without knowing.

Without realizing it.

Alexander picked up the phone again.

This time, he called Daniel.

“I need you to do something for me.”

Daniel was silent for a moment before answering.

“That sounds serious.”

“It is.”

“What do you need?”

“From now on, any document related to the property survey goes through you before it reaches Helena.”

“Why?”

“Because I want to reduce the number of people with access to the information.”

Daniel realized there was more behind the explanation.

“Alexander, what's going on?”

“I can't tell you yet.”

“Are you serious?”

“Very.”

Daniel fell silent.

“Are you trying to protect her?”

Alexander did not answer immediately.

“I'm trying to make sure she isn't involved in something that has nothing to do with her.”

Daniel took a deep breath.

“And you think she's going to accept that without asking questions?”

“No.”

“Then you know you're creating another problem.”

Alexander closed his eyes.

“I know.”

When he hung up, he realized Daniel was right. Helena would not accept being kept at a distance without an explanation. And the more Alexander tried to protect her by hiding information, the greater her suspicion would become.

But he saw no other option.

That afternoon, Helena left the office early. She did not want to admit that she was avoiding Alexander, but that was exactly what she was doing. She took the elevator down to the lobby and walked through the main entrance, trying not to look around. Her phone vibrated inside her bag.

She stopped on the sidewalk.

It was another message from the unknown number.

“If you really want to know what's happening, come tomorrow at seven.”

Below it was an address.

Helena recognized the location.

It was a small café a few blocks from the historic district, one of the few still operating in an old building that would be included in the second phase of the revitalization.

She read the message again.

Then she put her phone away.

She did not know who would be waiting for her. She did not know whether the person was telling the truth. She did not know whether it was a trap, an attempt at manipulation, or simply someone trying to use her name to hurt Alexander.

But now there was a difference.

She no longer wanted answers from Alexander.

Not because she had completely stopped trusting him, but because she was beginning to understand that he would never tell her what he believed he could hide in order to protect her.

And Helena was no longer willing to keep accepting silence as an answer.

That night, Alexander received another call while he was at the hospital, sitting beside his father. Richard was asleep, and the machines around him kept the room immersed in a succession of quiet, regular sounds. Alexander stepped into the hallway before answering.

“Yes?”

The voice on the other end spoke quietly.

“They found the person who was following Helena.”

Alexander felt his entire body tense.

“Who?”

“We don't know the name yet.”

“Then how do you know it's the same person?”

“Because we found images from the cameras near the building.”

Alexander took a deep breath.

“Where is the person now?”

“Gone.”

“And Helena?”

“She is safe. At least for now.”

Alexander closed his eyes.

“Don't say ‘for now.’”

“Alexander...”

“I want someone monitoring the entrances to her building.”

“That could attract attention.”

“I don't care.”

He hung up and remained standing in the hallway.

That was when he heard his father's voice behind him.

“You're trying to protect her.”

Alexander turned.

Richard was awake.

“Dad, you should rest.”

“Answer me.”

Alexander returned to the room.

“I don't want to involve her.”

Richard watched him for a few seconds.

“Then you've already involved her.”

Alexander remained silent.

“You think you can keep someone safe by hiding the truth,” Richard continued. “But secrets don't protect anyone forever.”

“I don't have a choice.”

“We always have choices.”

Alexander looked at his father.

“And what would you do?”

Richard took a long moment before answering.

“I would have told the truth before someone else had the opportunity to tell it for me.”

Alexander felt a shiver run through his body.

“What do you know?”

Richard closed his eyes again.

“More than I should have told you years ago.”

Alexander moved closer to the bed.

“Dad.”

But Richard did not answer.

The monitor continued its regular sounds while Alexander remained beside the bed, trying to understand what the sentence meant. For the first time, he realized that perhaps he had been looking for the answer in the wrong place. For weeks, he had believed the danger was connected only to the succession and the recent leaks. Now he was beginning to suspect that this was merely the most visible part of a story that had begun long before he had assumed any responsibility within the company.

And somewhere in that story, Helena's name had appeared.

The next morning, at exactly seven, Helena entered the small café indicated in the message. She chose a table near the window, where she could watch the street without being completely exposed, and placed her phone on the table. She ordered a coffee and tried to appear calm, although every person who entered the establishment made her body tense for a few seconds.

Five minutes.

Ten.

Fifteen.

Then the door opened.

A woman entered.

Helena recognized her.

Not immediately by her face, but by the way she walked, the dark coat, and the folder she carried against her body. She was someone Helena had already seen inside the Blackwood building.

Someone she had never imagined she would meet there.

The woman looked around the café, found Helena, and walked toward her table.

“You came.”

Helena looked up.

“You said you knew something about Alexander.”

The woman pulled out the chair and sat down.

“I do.”

“Then tell me.”

She placed the folder on the table but did not open it.

“First, I need you to understand something.”

“What?”

The woman looked at her.

“The problem didn't begin with Alexander.”

Helena remained still.

“It began with his father.”

Helena's hand tightened slightly around the cup.

“Richard?”

The woman nodded.

“And if you really want to discover what's happening, you need to understand why some people are so interested in controlling what will happen to the Blackwood family.”

She opened the folder, and inside were copies of old documents. Helena looked at the first page. Richard Blackwood's name appeared at the top, but it was not alone. There was another name beside it, a name Helena knew and that should not have been there.

chapters.title: The Name in the Document
chapters.content:
Helena remained silent for several seconds, staring at the sheet in front of her, unable to fully understand what she was seeing. The document was old, yellowed around the edges, and had clearly been handled many times before reaching the hands of the woman sitting across from her. At the top were details concerning a real estate transaction carried out years earlier, involving several of the properties that were now part of the revitalization project. Helena recognized the addresses. They were the same properties that had appeared in recent surveys and that, according to current records, had only attracted commercial interest after the Blackwood project began to take shape. But that was not what made her heart race. It was the name directly below the list of representatives involved in the negotiation.

Daniel Morgan.

Helena read it again.

Then she read it once more.

There was no doubt.

The last name was the same. The first name was too.

She slowly raised her eyes.

“Daniel Morgan?”

The woman nodded.

“Yes.”

“The Daniel who works with me?”

“If there is another Daniel Morgan directly involved with Blackwood, I don't know him.”

Helena looked back at the document.

“This doesn't make sense.”

“I know.”

“He joined the project only a few weeks ago.”

“I know.”

“Then how does his name appear here?”

The woman rested her arms on the table and leaned slightly closer.

“That is the question I wanted you to ask.”

Helena felt a growing uneasiness in her chest.

“You knew he was working with me?”

“I knew.”

“And you still asked me to come here?”

“Especially because of that.”

She partially closed the folder.

“You need to understand that I'm not saying Daniel did anything.”

Helena frowned.

“But you just put his name in a document related to the Blackwood family.”

“I didn't put it there. The document already had it.”

“You know what I mean.”

The woman took a deep breath.

“Daniel may have nothing to do with this.”

Helena fell silent.

Somehow, the answer made her even more uncomfortable.

“Then why did you show it to me?”

“Because this document proves that someone with the Morgan surname was involved in a transaction that should have remained restricted. And because, years later, a Morgan appeared precisely in the project that is once again putting these properties at the center of attention.”

Helena placed both hands on the table.

“That could be a coincidence.”

“It could.”

“You don't seem to believe that.”

“I believe in documents.”

Helena looked at the sheet again. There were dates, amounts, registration numbers, and names of companies she had never heard of. At the bottom of the page, a signature appeared beside Daniel Morgan's name. The signature was old, but it did not seem to have been made by him. Helena was not certain what Daniel's signature looked like, but there was something about the shape of the letters that made her uneasy.

“That signature doesn't look like his.”

The woman smiled faintly.

“It isn't.”

Helena raised her eyes.

“Then why is his name here?”

“Because it isn't his signature.”

She turned the document over.

On the back was a handwritten note.

Helena brought the paper closer to her face.

“What does it say?”

“Read it.”

She managed to decipher a few words.

“Authorized representative.”

Then there was a reference to another person.

Helena frowned.

“Who is this?”

The woman did not answer immediately.

“It's Daniel's father.”

Helena remained still.

“You know his father?”

“I did.”

“He worked for the Blackwoods?”

“For several years.”

The information made Helena lean back slightly in her chair.

Daniel had never mentioned that. In all the conversations they had during the project, he had talked about his previous jobs, the cities where he had lived, the revitalization projects he had worked on, and even the things he did outside work. But he had never mentioned any connection between his family and the Blackwoods.

“Did he know I was working with Daniel?”

“Probably.”

“And Alexander?”

The woman looked away for a moment.

“Alexander knows that the Morgans were involved in old family business dealings.”

“And why didn't he ever tell me?”

“Because perhaps he didn't know everything.”

Helena felt a growing irritation.

“This is getting exhausting.”

“What is?”

“Finding out that everyone knows one part of the story and I'm the only person who seems to receive fragments.”

The woman watched her in silence.

“Alexander tried to keep you out of this.”

“I know.”

“Then you also know why he did it.”

Helena let out a humorless laugh.

“No. I only know that he says he's trying to protect me.”

“And you don't believe him?”

She thought for a few seconds.

“I believe he's trying to protect me. I don't know if I believe he's doing it the right way.”

The woman nodded slowly.

“That is an important difference.”

Helena looked back at the documents.

“What happened to Daniel's father?”

“He died a few years ago.”

“And the company?”

“It was shut down.”

“Then how did these documents reappear now?”

The woman did not answer.

Helena raised her eyes.

“You don't know?”

“I know someone started looking for these documents again a few months ago.”

“Who?”

“I haven't found out yet.”

“And that's why the information started leaking?”

“Maybe.”

Helena remained silent.

The café continued bustling around them, but the sound of the conversations seemed distant. Through the window, cars passed along the street and people hurried by, completely unaware of the conversation taking place inside. It was strange to realize how normally the world could continue functioning while a part of her life began taking on shapes she had never imagined.

“Why me?” Helena asked.

The woman took a few seconds before answering.

“Because you're close to Alexander.”

“That doesn't explain anything.”

“It explains more than you realize.”

“Then explain it.”

The woman closed the folder.

“You joined the project after some of these properties were reassessed. You gained access to information that few people outside the family had. You began working directly with Alexander. And shortly afterward, the leaks began.”

Helena felt a chill run down the back of her neck.

“Are you saying they think I have something to do with this?”

“No.”

“Then why are they watching me?”

“Because you may know something without realizing that you know it.”

Helena remained silent.

The sentence made uncomfortable sense. Since the beginning of the project, she had worked with documents, reports, and property assessments. She had access to enough information for someone to consider her a potential source, even though she had never imagined those details could have any value beyond her work itself.

“What exactly is so important about these properties?”

The woman opened the folder again and took out another sheet.

“Some of them were purchased years ago for very low prices.”

“I know.”

“No. You know that the historical values were low. What you don't know is why.”

Helena took the sheet.

There was a list of properties and acquisition prices. Some of the figures were absurdly lower than their current values.

“They knew the area would appreciate?”

“More than that.”

“What do you mean?”

“There was an urban development plan long before the current project existed.”

Helena raised her eyes.

“A city plan?”

“In part.”

“And the Blackwoods had access to it?”

“People connected to the Blackwoods did.”

Helena looked back at the documents.

“So someone bought the properties before the appreciation happened.”

“Exactly.”

“And afterward?”

“Some were sold. Others remained in the family's assets. And some passed through intermediary companies.”

Helena felt a weight in her stomach.

“Companies that don't appear in the current records.”

“Some of them.”

She leaned back in her chair.

“And what does Daniel have to do with this?”

The woman held her gaze.

“We don't know yet.”

“You just showed me his name.”

“His father's name.”

“Daniel Morgan appears on the document.”

“As the authorized representative of his father's company.”

Helena frowned.

“But he was very young.”

“Not necessarily.”

The woman pointed to the date.

Helena did the math in her head.

Daniel could have been just over twenty at the time. It was possible, although strange.

“You're saying he already worked with his father?”

“I'm saying his name was used.”

“That's different.”

“Very.”

Helena fell silent.

There was something about that distinction she could not ignore.

If Daniel had knowingly participated in an old transaction, it would change the way she saw him. But if someone had used his name, the story could be completely different.

“Do you think he knows?”

The woman closed the folder.

“I think you should ask him.”

Helena stood.

“And if he doesn't?”

“Then you'll have discovered one more person being kept in the dark.”

She picked up her bag.

“And if he does?”

The woman looked at her.

“Then you'll discover why he joined this particular project.”

Helena felt an immediate discomfort.

Daniel had been introduced as someone experienced, competent, and well suited to that phase of the work. Alexander had accepted his presence, although he had initially shown some discomfort. She had never considered that hiring him might have anything to do with the family's history.

Maybe she was seeing connections where none existed.

Maybe she wasn't.

Before leaving, Helena stopped.

“Who are you?”

The woman raised her eyes.

“My name is Victoria Hale.”

The name meant nothing to Helena.

“And what is your relationship with the Blackwoods?”

Victoria remained silent for several seconds.

“I worked for Richard.”

“When?”

“Before Alexander took over most of the business.”

“And why did you leave?”

Victoria closed the folder.

“Because I discovered some things I wasn't supposed to discover.”

Helena waited.

“That isn't exactly an answer.”

“It's the answer I can give you today.”

Helena held her gaze.

“And why should I trust you?”

Victoria smiled faintly.

“You shouldn't.”

The answer surprised Helena.

“Then why am I here?”

“Because, for the first time, you're asking the right question.”

Helena did not answer.

She picked up her bag and left.

The journey back to the office was silent. She could have called Alexander. She could have asked him directly about Daniel, Richard, the documents, and the old connection between the families. But she decided not to. Not yet.

She needed to know how much of it was true.

When she arrived at the Blackwood building, she found Daniel in the lobby.

He smiled as soon as he saw her.

“Where were you?”

Helena stopped.

“I had something to take care of.”

“Everything okay?”

She studied him for a few seconds.

It was difficult to look at him the same way after seeing that document. Daniel seemed exactly as he always had. Calm, approachable, with the easy manner of conversation that had made her feel comfortable around him from the first days. There was nothing in his expression that revealed any secret.

Maybe that meant nothing.

Or maybe it meant everything.

“Daniel.”

“Yes?”

“Can I ask you something?”

He smiled.

“Of course.”

“Did your father work for Blackwood?”

The smile disappeared.

Not completely.

Just enough.

Helena noticed.

Daniel took a second longer than usual before answering.

“Why are you asking?”

“Because I found his name in an old document.”

Daniel went still.

“Where?”

“Does that matter?”

“It matters a lot.”

Helena felt the confirmation before hearing any explanation.

“So you knew.”

“No.”

“You didn't know he worked for Blackwood?”

Daniel took a deep breath.

“I knew he had business dealings with the company.”

“Business dealings?”

“Some.”

“How many?”

“Helena...”

“How many?”

He looked around the lobby before answering.

“I don't know.”

“You never mentioned it.”

“Because I didn't think it was relevant.”

“Your father having worked for the family at the center of the project you just joined doesn't seem relevant?”

Daniel ran a hand over the back of his neck.

“I didn't join the project because of him.”

“I didn't ask that.”

“But that's what you're thinking.”

Helena crossed her arms.

“Then tell me what I should think.”

Daniel remained silent.

“My father had problems with the Blackwoods,” he finally said. “I don't know all the details. When I was younger, he didn't talk about work at home. After he died, I found some documents, but I never managed to understand exactly what had happened.”

Helena felt the tension ease only slightly.

“And your name?”

“What about my name?”

“It appears on one of them.”

Daniel went pale.

“That isn't possible.”

“I saw it.”

“Where?”

Helena hesitated.

She did not want to reveal Victoria's existence.

“In an old folder.”

Daniel looked at her.

“Helena, I never signed anything for Blackwood.”

“I didn't say you did.”

“Then someone used my name.”

She studied his expression.

He did not seem to be lying.

But Helena had already learned that, in that circle, appearances did not mean much.

“How long have you known Alexander?”

Daniel frowned.

“I met Alexander professionally a few years ago, but I never worked directly with him before this project.”

“And your father?”

Daniel looked away.

“My father knew Richard.”

The information fell between them.

Helena remained silent.

“Were they close?”

“I don't know.”

“You don't know?”

“My father never talked about him.”

Daniel took a deep breath.

“All I know is that, after a certain period, he became very different. More reserved. More suspicious. When I asked what had happened, he said that some people didn't like it when someone asked too many questions.”

Helena felt a chill.

“And you never tried to find out what happened?”

“I tried.”

“And?”

“I couldn't.”

She stared at him.

For the first time, Daniel seemed as lost as she was.

“Do you think this is connected to the project?”

Daniel took a moment before answering.

“I think it could be.”

Helena nodded.

“So do I.”

They remained silent.

Then Daniel asked:

“Does Alexander know?”

Helena did not answer.

Daniel understood.

“He knows something.”

“He knows more than he's told me.”

“That isn't surprising.”

Helena raised her eyes.

“You seem to know him better than I thought.”

“I don't.”

“Then why did you say that?”

Daniel gave a small smile, but there was no humor in it.

“Because men like Alexander don't spend years building empires without learning how to keep secrets.”

Before Helena could answer, the elevator doors opened.

Alexander stepped out.

His eyes immediately found the two of them.

First Daniel.

Then Helena.

He stopped.

There was something in Alexander's expression that Helena had never seen before. It was not merely surprise. It was recognition.

As if, in that instant, he had realized exactly what they were discussing.

Alexander walked toward them.

“What happened?”

Helena kept her eyes on him.

“Nothing.”

“Helena.”

“We were talking.”

Alexander looked at Daniel.

“About?”

Daniel answered before she could.

“My father.”

Alexander went completely still.

For several seconds, no one said anything.

Then Alexander looked back at Helena.

“Where did you hear that name?”

The question confirmed everything she needed to know.

He knew the story.

“Then you know who he is.”

Alexander took a deep breath.

“Helena, we need to talk.”

“No.”

He looked surprised.

“No?”

“Not here.”

Alexander studied her face.

“Then where?”

She hesitated.

For a moment, she considered telling him she did not want to speak with him. She considered letting him discover that she already knew part of the truth. But there was something in his expression that made her stop. It was not irritation. It was concern.

And for the first time, Helena realized that Alexander was not simply afraid that she would discover a secret.

He was afraid of what might happen after she did.

“Your office,” she said.

Alexander nodded.

Daniel took a step back.

“I'll let you two talk.”

Helena looked at him.

“Daniel.”

He stopped.

“I don't think you're lying.”

Daniel held her gaze.

“Thank you.”

He walked away.

Alexander waited until Daniel disappeared down the corridor before speaking.

“You shouldn't have looked into this.”

Helena stared at him.

“I didn't.”

“Then how did you find it?”

“Someone came to me.”

His expression changed.

“Who?”

“Victoria Hale.”

Alexander became completely still.

Helena noticed immediately.

“You know that name.”

He took several seconds before answering.

“I do.”

“Who is she?”

Alexander ran a hand over his face.

“Someone who worked for my father.”

“She showed me documents.”

“Which ones?”

“Documents about properties, companies, and an old transaction involving your father and Daniel's father.”

Alexander closed his eyes.

“My God.”

“What does that mean?”

He moved toward the desk but did not sit.

“It means you're much closer to this than I wanted.”

Helena felt her irritation return.

“Finally.”

Alexander looked up.

“What?”

“Finally you're admitting it.”

“I never said there was nothing happening.”

“You simply never said what it was.”

He remained silent.

Helena took a deep breath.

“You knew about Daniel's father?”

“Yes.”

“Since when?”

“Before he joined the project.”

She felt a flash of indignation.

“And you still allowed him to join?”

“I had no reason to believe Daniel was involved.”

“But you knew his family had a history with yours.”

“Yes.”

“And you didn't think it was important to tell me?”

“I didn't want to put you in the middle of this.”

Helena laughed without humor.

“Alexander, I'm already in the middle of it.”

He did not answer.

“Someone is following me.”

Alexander immediately raised his head.

“Who told you that?”

Helena realized her mistake.

“So you knew.”

“Helena...”

“You knew I was being followed.”

“I knew someone was watching you.”

Her heart began to race.

“And you didn't tell me.”

“Because I was trying to find out who it was.”

“While I was leaving the building without knowing anything.”

“I was protecting you.”

“No.”

Alexander frowned.

“No?”

“You were deciding for me.”

He remained silent.

Helena felt her eyes burn, but she did not allow the emotion to alter her voice.

“I don't need you to choose what I am allowed to know.”

“If you knew everything, you might do something impulsive.”

“And if I know nothing, I'll keep walking in the dark.”

Alexander moved closer.

“I don't want you to be afraid.”

“I already am.”

The sentence made Alexander stop.

Helena took a deep breath.

“Not for myself.”

He watched her.

“For you.”

The silence between them changed.

For several seconds, neither spoke.

Alexander looked away.

“My father is very ill.”

“I know.”

“And there's a succession dispute that began long before me. There are missing documents, companies that were used to move money, and people who had access to information that should have remained confidential. We're still trying to understand how far it goes.”

Helena remained still.

“And the project?”

“It's part of it.”

“How?”

“The properties we're revitalizing were acquired for very low prices years ago. Some of those acquisitions happened before any public plan to increase the area's value existed. Someone knew that area would become important.”

“Your father?”

“Maybe.”

“And Daniel?”

Alexander hesitated.

“Daniel's father was involved in some of those transactions.”

“And Daniel?”

“I don't know.”

Helena studied his face.

“Do you trust him?”

Alexander took a moment before answering.

“I don't know whom to trust anymore.”

The sincerity of the statement struck her unexpectedly.

Alexander walked to the window.

“And that's exactly what worries me.”

Helena moved closer.

“What else aren't you telling me?”

He remained with his back to her.

“One thing.”

She waited.

Alexander finally turned around.

“Victoria's name appears in old documents related to my father.”

Helena fell silent.

“She disappeared from the company years ago,” he continued. “After that, no one knew exactly where she was. I never understood why she came back now.”

“Maybe she knows something.”

“Maybe.”

“And maybe she was the one sending the messages.”

Alexander looked at her.

“What messages?”

Helena hesitated.

Then she realized there was no reason to hide them anymore.

She took out her phone, opened the conversation, and handed it to him.

Alexander read it.

His expression changed.

“When did you receive this?”

“Yesterday.”

“Why didn't you tell me?”

Helena held his gaze.

“You just asked why I don't trust you.”

Alexander slowly handed the phone back.

He had no answer.

Helena put the phone away.

“I think we're in a situation where neither of us can keep hiding things.”

Alexander remained silent.

She walked toward the door.

“Helena.”

She stopped.

“Yes?”

He seemed hesitant.

“I never wanted you to become involved in this.”

“I know.”

“And I don't regret trying to protect you.”

She looked at him.

“I just wish you had trusted me enough to tell me.”

Alexander held her gaze for several seconds.

“Maybe I didn't know how.”

Helena opened the door.

“Then learn.”

She left.

Alexander remained alone.

Outside, Helena walked down the corridor, trying to organize everything she had just discovered. Daniel had a connection to the family's past. Victoria had reappeared after years. Richard knew more than he was saying. Alexander had admitted that there were people watching his movements. And at the center of everything were the properties in the project, the same ones she had been analyzing for months without imagining that they carried a much larger history.

When she reached the elevator, her phone vibrated again.

Helena looked at the screen.

It was not Victoria.

It was a different unknown number.

The message contained only a photograph.

Helena opened it.

It was an old image, apparently taken from some archive.

Richard Blackwood stood beside two men.

One of them was Daniel's father.

The other was someone Helena recognized immediately.

It was Alexander himself.

But there was an impossible detail.

The photograph was dated almost fifteen years before Helena had even known his name.

Helena felt the blood drain from her face.

On the back of the image was a handwritten sentence:

“Ask Alexander what happened that night.”

Helena stood frozen in front of the closed elevator doors, phone in her hands, with the feeling that she had just discovered that the story everyone was trying to hide had not begun with her.

Perhaps it had not even begun with Alexander.

But for the first time, she was beginning to suspect that he knew exactly where that story had begun.

And perhaps he also knew why someone was willing to do anything to stop her from discovering how it ended.

chapters.title: The Night That Stayed Behind
chapters.content:
Helena remained standing in front of the elevator for a few seconds, her phone still in her hands and the photograph open on the screen. The movement of the people around her continued as usual, employees crossed the lobby, conversations began and ended, and the sound of elevators announcing each floor blended with the quiet hum of the building, but none of it seemed to truly reach her attention. Her eyes remained fixed on Richard Blackwood, on the man she had recognized as Daniel’s father and, above all, on the younger figure of Alexander standing beside them. The date was clearly recorded in the lower corner of the photograph. Almost fifteen years earlier. Helena did the calculation again, even though she knew she did not need to. Alexander had already been an adult at the time. There was no possibility that this was a childhood photograph or some casual encounter that could easily be explained. He was there because he was part of that story.

She enlarged the image.

Something had been written on the back, but the photograph she had received showed only the front. The message told her to ask Alexander what had happened that night, but it did not say where the photograph had been taken, who had taken it, or why someone had decided to send it now. Helena felt the same mixture of anger and unease that had accompanied her recent discoveries. For weeks, Alexander had insisted that some things did not concern her, that he was trying to protect her, and that he could not tell her everything yet. Now she was beginning to understand that perhaps he had not merely been hiding recent information. Perhaps there was an entire part of his life he had never spoken about. And as much as the discovery made her suspicious, there was something even harder to ignore: the expression on Alexander’s face in the photograph was not the expression of the controlled man she knew. There was a tension in his features that seemed to belong to someone much younger, but also much more troubled than she had ever seen him.

Helena put the phone back in her bag and decided she would not ask him by message. She did not want a prepared answer, nor a few carefully chosen sentences meant to close the subject. If Alexander truly knew what had happened that night, she wanted to see him when she asked. She wanted to watch his eyes, his reaction, the silences between one word and another. After everything that had happened between them, perhaps this was the first time Helena was unwilling to accept an incomplete answer.

She found him a short while later on the top floor of the building. The door to his office was slightly open, and Alexander stood by the window with his phone against his ear. Helena stopped in the hallway when she heard him speaking in a low voice, different from his usual tone.

—No. I don't want to delay this any longer.

There was a pause.

—If my father can't speak, we need to find the documents before someone else does.

Another pause.

—I don't care how long it takes. Find out who authorized that transfer.

Helena remained still.

Alexander ended the call a few seconds later and, when he turned around, noticed her presence. His expression changed immediately.

—Helena.

She entered the office and closed the door behind her.

—We need to talk.

Alexander placed his phone on the desk.

—Judging by your tone, I imagine we do.

She took the phone from her bag and placed the photograph on the desk, face up.

Alexander looked at it.

The silence that followed was so complete that Helena could hear the faint sound of the air conditioner.

He did not ask where the photograph had come from.

He did not ask who had sent it.

He simply stared at the image.

And that was precisely what confirmed her suspicion.

—You know this photograph.

Alexander took a few seconds to answer.

—Yes.

Helena felt her chest tighten.

—Then tell me.

He ran a hand along his jaw and looked toward the window.

—I knew this photograph still existed.

—Where was it taken?

—At a property my father owned in the countryside.

—When?

—Fifteen years ago.

—And what were you doing there?

Alexander remained silent.

Helena took a step forward.

—I'm asking what happened that night.

He finally looked back at her.

—Did you receive the photograph with this sentence?

—Yes.

—Did someone write something on the back?

—I didn't see the back.

Alexander frowned.

—Then whoever sent it didn't want you to have the complete photograph.

—What does that mean?

He took a deep breath.

—It means whoever is doing this knows the story, but doesn't necessarily want you to know the whole truth. They want you to discover just enough to keep searching.

Helena felt a surge of irritation.

—Do you realize how that sounds?

—I do.

—Because it sounds exactly like what you've been doing to me for weeks.

The words struck him. Alexander did not try to defend himself immediately.

—I know.

Helena crossed her arms.

—Then stop.

He remained silent for a few seconds before walking to the desk and picking up the photograph.

—Back then, my father was negotiating several properties in the area. I had just started taking on a larger part of the business, and I attended some meetings because he wanted to prepare me for the future.

—And Daniel's father?

—He worked as an intermediary in some of those negotiations.

—Was Victoria there?

Alexander looked up.

—Not that night.

Helena watched his face.

—Are you sure?

—I am.

—Then who was?

Alexander placed the photograph back on the desk.

—My father, Daniel's father, me, and one other person.

Helena felt the tension increase.

—Who?

He hesitated.

—My brother.

It was the first time Alexander had mentioned his brother directly to her, and Helena immediately noticed that there was something about the answer he did not want to explore further.

—And what happened?

Alexander took a deep breath.

—An argument.

—About what?

—Money.

—Only that?

He looked away.

—No.

Helena waited.

Alexander slowly walked toward the window.

—That night, we discovered that a company connected to the negotiations had received money from an account that shouldn't have existed. My father said it wasn't his responsibility. Daniel's father disagreed.

—Why?

—Because he knew the company had been created to hide certain transactions.

Helena felt a chill.

—And your father knew?

—I believe so.

—You believe?

Alexander closed his eyes for a moment.

—I was in my twenties, Helena. At that time, I still believed my father told me everything.

She moved closer.

—And he didn't.

—No.

The answer was quiet.

Helena looked at the man standing before her. For the first time, Alexander did not seem to be trying to control the conversation. There was a vulnerability in his expression that did not fit the man who usually entered any room as though he already knew exactly what to do.

—What happened after the argument?

—Daniel's father threatened to walk away from the deal.

—And did he?

—Not that night.

Alexander remained silent for a few seconds.

—After that, there was an accident.

Helena felt her entire body go still.

—What kind of accident?

—His car went off the road while he was driving home.

It took her a few seconds to understand.

—Did he die?

Alexander nodded.

—Not that night. He was hospitalized for several weeks. He survived for several years afterward, but he never worked for Blackwood again.

Helena breathed slowly.

—And you never told Daniel?

—I didn't know how much he knew.

—You knew he didn't know?

—I knew his father had never told him everything.

—Then why did you let Daniel join the project?

Alexander looked at her.

—Because Daniel isn't his father.

Helena held his gaze.

—You believe he isn't involved?

—I want to believe that.

—That's not the same thing.

—I know.

She looked back at the photograph.

—Why were you there?

Alexander hesitated.

—Because my father wanted me to learn how the business really worked.

—And did you learn?

A sad smile appeared on his face.

—I learned that some things can be very different from what they appear to be.

Helena remained silent.

There was a difference between hearing Alexander talk about his father as a powerful man and hearing that same person admit that, when he was young, he had discovered he did not completely know his own family. Perhaps that was one of the reasons he tried to control everything now. Perhaps he had learned too early that trusting people meant taking risks.

—Were you afraid that night? —she asked.

Alexander did not answer immediately.

When he finally spoke, his voice was quieter.

—Yes.

The sincerity of the answer disarmed Helena.

—Of what?

—Of losing my father. Of losing control of the company. Of discovering that the people I trusted weren't who I thought they were.

He looked back at her.

—Some of those things ended up happening.

Helena felt her anger diminish, although it did not disappear completely.

—And now you're doing to me what they did to you.

Alexander stood still.

—Maybe.

—You think hiding things will keep me from getting hurt.

—I do.

—But it only means I don't know who to trust.

He slowly nodded.

—I know.

The silence between them stretched.

Helena looked away.

—I'm still hurt by you.

Alexander did not pretend he didn't know what she meant.

—I know.

—After that night at the reception, you acted as though nothing had happened.

—Because I was afraid.

She looked back at him.

—Afraid of what?

Alexander moved closer but stopped at a respectful distance.

—Of wanting that more than I should.

Helena felt her heart race.

He continued:

—I tried to convince myself the kiss had been a mistake. I tried to go back to work, act as before, and keep everything under control. But I couldn't.

Helena said nothing.

—When I realized you were being watched, I thought pushing you away would be the only way to keep you safe. I thought that if you were away from me, you'd be away from all of this.

—And you thought I'd rather be pushed away than know the truth?

—No.

—Then why did you do it?

Alexander took a deep breath.

—Because I didn't know how to do anything else.

Helena felt her eyes fill with emotion, but she did not look away.

—You could have trusted me.

—I should have trusted you.

He took another step closer.

—I'm sorry.

There was no arrogance in his voice. No attempt to justify what he had done. Only an honesty Helena was not used to receiving from him.

—I don't want you to apologize just because you're afraid of losing me —she said.

Alexander held her gaze.

—I'm not only afraid of losing you now.

She remained silent.

—I was already afraid before.

The words remained between them.

Helena did not know exactly what to say. She had imagined that conversation many times, but never like this. In her imagination, Alexander would have been defensive, trying to hide some piece of information, and she would leave the room more determined than when she entered. Instead, she was standing before a man who finally seemed willing to admit that he did not have all the answers either.

She moved closer until she stood in front of him.

—I can't promise I'll trust you immediately.

—I don't expect you to promise that.

—And I won't forget what happened.

—Neither will I.

Helena took a deep breath.

—But I also don't want to keep pretending there isn't something between us.

Alexander remained still.

—There isn't? —he asked.

She shook her head.

—There is.

His expression changed.

—Helena...

—I just don't know what to do with it yet.

Alexander smiled faintly, almost relieved.

—Neither do I.

She let out a small laugh.

—For the first time, you don't seem to have an answer.

—It's a new experience.

Her smile appeared before she could stop it.

Alexander watched her.

—I missed that.

—Missed what?

—You smiling at me.

Helena lowered her eyes for a moment.

—You could have avoided losing it.

—I know.

He slowly raised his hand but stopped before touching her.

Helena noticed the gesture.

After a few seconds, she was the one who closed the distance between them.

Alexander touched her face carefully, as though he were still silently asking whether it was allowed. Helena did not pull away. Instead, she closed her eyes when his fingers touched her skin.

The kiss came slowly.

Different from the first.

There was no surprise, impulse, or hesitation filled with fear. There was choice. Alexander moved closer carefully, and Helena responded, feeling all the tension of the past weeks lose its strength for a few moments. When they pulled apart, they remained close, still silent, as though neither wanted to be the first to break the moment.

—Was that a mistake too? —she asked softly.

Alexander smiled.

—No.

—Are you sure?

—This time, I am.

Helena rested her forehead against his chest for a few seconds.

—I'm still angry.

—You can stay angry.

—Don't get used to it.

—I don't intend to.

She smiled again, but soon lifted her face.

—We have a problem.

—I know.

—No, Alexander. We have several.

He let out a quiet laugh.

—I know that too.

Helena stepped back slightly.

—The photograph, Victoria, your father, Daniel, the documents... it's all connected.

—Probably.

—And someone wants me to find out.

Alexander became serious again.

—Yes.

—Then let's find out.

He looked at her.

—We?

—We.

The word seemed to surprise him.

Helena noticed.

—If you really want me to stay safe, stop trying to do everything alone.

Alexander nodded.

—All right.

—And don't hide anything else from me.

—I will try.

She raised an eyebrow.

—That wasn't a very convincing answer.

—Then I'll do better.

He took her hand.

—I won't hide anything else from you.

Helena squeezed his fingers.

—Now that's better.

For a few moments, they remained like that, close to one another, without needing to fill the silence. But the calm did not last long. Alexander's phone vibrated on the desk.

He released her hand and picked up the device.

The message was from his brother.

**We found the file from the night of the accident.**

Alexander opened the rest.

**There is a witness.**

Below it was a name.

He went still.

Helena noticed the change in his expression.

—What is it?

Alexander handed her the phone.

Helena read it.

And felt her heart stop for a moment.

The witness's name was Victoria Hale.

She looked up.

—So she didn't come back by accident.

Alexander shook his head.

—No.

Helena looked at the message again.

—She was there that night.

—It seems so.

—And she knows what happened.

Alexander took the phone back.

—Then it's time to find out why she waited fifteen years to tell us.

Helena nodded.

But before either of them could say anything else, her phone vibrated.

It was a new message.

This time, there was only one sentence:

**“Now that Alexander has finally told you, ask him who was driving the car.”**

Helena slowly looked up. Alexander read the message over her shoulder, and the color drained from his face.

And for the first time since she had begun the investigation, Helena realized there was a part of that night Alexander had not told her. Not because he had forgotten. But because he still wasn't ready to say who had been behind the wheel.

chapters.title: What Alexander Hid
chapters.content:
Helena did not take her eyes off the phone screen. The message remained there, simple and cruel in the way it managed to turn everything Alexander had just told her into a new question. For several minutes, she could think of nothing except that sentence: who was driving the car? The question did not seem intended to reveal just any piece of information. There was something behind it, a precise intention, as though the person who had sent the message knew exactly which part of the story Alexander had omitted and had waited for the right moment to expose it. Helena slowly raised her eyes to him. Alexander remained motionless, the phone still in his hand, but his expression had changed completely. It was no longer merely concern. There was guilt. An old, deeply buried guilt that seemed to have been awakened by the question.

—Was it you? Helena asked.

Alexander closed his eyes for a moment.

He did not answer.

And that silence was enough.

Helena felt her heart tighten, but she did not look away. For weeks, she had asked him for the truth. She had complained about his omissions, the decisions he made on her behalf, the way there always seemed to be a part of the story she could not access. Now, finally, she was standing before that part. And although a small part of her wanted Alexander to deny it, another already knew he would not.

—Alexander.

He placed the phone on the desk.

—Yes.

The word came quietly.

Helena remained still, trying to absorb the answer. She had not imagined exactly this. She had thought of Richard, of Daniel's father, perhaps Alexander's brother. But not him. Suddenly, the photograph took on another meaning. Alexander had not merely been present that night. He had been directly involved in what happened afterward.

—You were driving?

—Yes.

Helena took a deep breath.

—Then tell me everything.

Alexander ran a hand through his hair and moved a few steps away, as though he needed space to organize a memory he had spent years trying to keep buried. Helena did not interrupt him. For the first time, she understood that this was not a conversation that could be rushed. There were things Alexander was not simply choosing to tell. There were things he would have to face as he spoke.

—That night, my father argued with Daniel's father because of the intermediary companies. I didn't understand everything that was happening, but I knew money was moving through channels that didn't appear in the official documents. My father wanted to end the conversation. Daniel's father wanted to take the records to the authorities.

Helena felt her stomach tighten.

—He wanted to report your father?

—I don't know if he wanted to report my father specifically. I think he wanted to expose the scheme. At the time, I still believed my father might not know everything. Today, I'm not so sure.

Alexander paused before continuing.

—After the argument, my father asked me to drive Daniel's father into town. He was too angry to drive and didn't want him leaving alone. I agreed. I thought it would be a short trip.

—And did you talk?

—Yes.

—About what?

Alexander looked back at her.

—About my father.

Helena waited.

—He told me I needed to be careful. He said there were things I didn't understand and that, if I intended to take over the family business, I needed to learn to ask questions before accepting answers. At the time, I thought he was simply trying to turn me against my father.

—But he wasn't.

—No.

Alexander took a deep breath.

—He handed me a folder before getting into the car. He said those documents could prove that some properties had been acquired using inside information. I didn't understand the extent of it. I only knew my father would be furious if he found out I had the documents.

Helena slowly moved closer.

—Do you still have that folder?

Alexander took a few seconds to answer.

—No.

—What happened to it?

—It disappeared after the accident.

Helena felt a chill.

—Do you know how?

—No.

—But someone took it.

—Probably.

She fell silent. Alexander placed both hands on the desk.

—The trip should have taken a little over twenty minutes. We didn't even make it halfway.

—What happened?

—The brakes failed.

Helena felt her chest tighten.

—Failed?

—The pedal stopped responding. I tried to slow down, but the car didn't react. The road was wet, and there was a curve a few meters ahead. I tried to control the vehicle, but we lost control.

He stopped. Helena noticed that his fingers were trembling.

—And the accident?

—The car left the road and crashed into a concrete barrier. I was wearing my seat belt. So was he. I walked away almost unharmed. He was seriously injured.

—Did you call for help?

Alexander nodded.

—I stayed beside him until the ambulance arrived. He was conscious for a few minutes.

—What did he say?

Alexander looked away.

—He told me not to trust my father.

Helena felt a heavy silence settle between them.

—That was the last thing he said to me that night.

—And then?

—Then he was taken to the hospital.

Alexander took a deep breath.

—When my father arrived, he didn't ask first if I was all right. He asked about the folder.

Helena closed her eyes for a moment.

—So he knew.

—He may have known there were documents. I don't know how.

—And what did you tell him?

—I said I didn't have anything.

—You lied?

—Yes.

The answer came without hesitation. Helena watched him.

—Why?

—Because in that moment I realized that what had happened might not have been an accident.

A chill ran across her skin.

—You thought your father had the brakes tampered with?

Alexander remained silent for a few seconds.

—I didn't know who had done it. But I knew someone wanted those documents.

—And you never told anyone?

—I told my brother.

—And him?

—He said I needed to leave it behind.

Helena felt indignation rising inside her.

—And did you?

Alexander gave a bitter laugh.

—I tried.

He moved closer to her.

—After that accident, my father took control of everything. Daniel's father survived, but withdrew from the business. The documents disappeared. The intermediary company was shut down. And, not long afterward, other companies began appearing under different names, moving the same assets.

Helena remained silent.

—And Victoria?

—She discovered part of it.

—Was she there that night?

—Not at the time of the accident.

—But she was involved.

—Yes.

Alexander picked up his phone again and opened an old photograph.

—She worked in the legal department at the time. She was one of the people who noticed that the records were being altered after the accident.

Helena moved closer to look.

—So she knew.

—She knew something was wrong. I don't know if she knew everything.

—And why did she disappear?

—Because after she started asking questions, she was removed.

Helena looked back at him.

—By your father?

—Yes.

The answer was immediate. She felt a strange sadness.

—Alexander, you carried this alone for fifteen years.

—Not completely.

—But almost.

He remained silent. Helena lightly touched his arm.

—Why didn't you ever tell me?

Alexander looked at her hand before meeting her eyes again.

—Because I didn't want you to look at me and see that boy.

—What boy?

—The one who was driving when everything happened.

Helena felt her heart tighten.

—Alexander...

—I know I didn't cause the accident. I know the brakes were sabotaged. I know there was nothing I could have done to prevent it. But for years I thought that if I'd driven more slowly, chosen another road, noticed some warning... anything could have been different.

—You can't carry responsibility for something that wasn't your fault.

—I know that rationally.

—And emotionally?

He smiled without humor.

—It's more complicated.

Helena stood before him.

—Do you think the accident was planned?

Alexander nodded.

—Now I'm certain.

—How?

—Because we found maintenance records for the car.

He picked up a folder lying on the desk and opened several pages.

—The brakes had been inspected two days earlier. The report said they were in perfect condition. After the accident, someone tried to alter the record to make it look as though there had been an existing problem.

Helena quickly read through the documents.

—Who performed the inspection?

—A company that no longer exists.

—The same intermediary company?

—No. But the owner had ties to it.

She raised her eyes.

—So someone tried to cover up the accident.

—Yes.

—And the documents you had with you?

—They were about the properties.

Helena thought about the project again.

—The same properties we're revitalizing now.

Alexander nodded.

—Exactly.

Everything was beginning to fit together. Not perfectly; there were still too many gaps, but for the first time the story seemed to have a continuous thread. The properties had been purchased before their value increased. Intermediary companies had moved money. Daniel's father had discovered something. A folder had disappeared after a suspicious accident. Victoria had found documents years later. And now, with the revitalization project bringing those properties back into the center of attention, someone seemed determined to prevent the past from being uncovered.

Helena closed the folder.

—So that's why they're after me.

—Partly.

—Because I have access to the project documents.

—Yes.

—And because I'm with you.

Alexander fell silent.

Helena understood the answer without needing to hear it.

—That means the problem isn't only the project.

—It never was.

She took a deep breath.

—And you knew that when you kissed me.

Alexander lowered his eyes.

—I knew there were risks.

—And you still brought me to that reception.

—Yes.

—Why?

He took a moment to answer.

—Because that night I wanted something that had nothing to do with the company, my father, or the succession.

Helena remained silent.

—I wanted you with me.

The sincerity of the answer tightened her chest. Alexander moved closer.

—Maybe it was selfish.

—It was.

He accepted the answer with a small smile.

—But it was the first time in a long time that I did something simply because I wanted to.

Helena lowered her eyes.

—And then you regretted it.

—No.

She looked back at him.

—Then why did you push me away?

—Because the next day I discovered you were being watched.

Helena went still.

—Was that when you received the photograph?

Alexander nodded.

—Yes.

—And you decided it would be better to make me believe the kiss meant nothing.

—I thought that if you were angry with me, maybe you would stay away.

She let out a small laugh.

—You really don't know me.

—I'm starting to.

Helena shook her head.

—You're terrible at this.

—At protecting you?

—At hiding what you feel.

Alexander smiled.

—Maybe.

He took a step toward her but did not touch her immediately.

—I don't want to hide anymore.

Helena remained silent.

—I spent weeks trying to convince myself that what I feel for you could be put aside. That it was only attraction, admiration, maybe the result of spending so much time together. But it isn't. I'm in love with you, Helena.

She felt her heart race, but she did not answer.

Not because she had nothing to say. There were too many things inside her at that moment. Alexander's past, the accident, Daniel's father, Victoria, the properties, the documents, the threat and, in the middle of all of it, the feeling she herself was still trying to understand. His confession did not seem to demand an immediate answer. For the first time, Alexander was not trying to control what would happen next.

He had simply told her the truth.

Helena raised her eyes and looked at him for several seconds. Alexander did not look away. There was no impatient expectation in his expression, only a vulnerability she had never seen in him quite like this.

She took a step forward.

Alexander waited.

Helena placed her hand against his face and kissed him.

The kiss began slowly, almost like a silent confirmation that she had heard everything he had said, but still needed time to discover what those words meant inside her. Alexander held her waist carefully and kissed her back, without rushing, without trying to turn the moment into a promise. There was desire, but there was also something deeper in the way he held her close, as if he had finally understood that he did not need to decide for her what their relationship should be.

When they pulled apart, they remained close. Helena still had her hand against his face. Alexander touched her hand and held it for a few seconds.

Neither of them spoke. There was no need. Helena closed her eyes for a moment and took a deep breath. She was not yet ready to put everything she felt into words. Perhaps because she had just discovered a part of Alexander's life that changed the way she saw the man standing before her. Perhaps because she was beginning to realize that her own feelings had gone far beyond the irritation, curiosity, and attraction she had initially tried to treat as an inconvenient consequence of their time together.

Or perhaps because some answers needed time before they could become words.

Alexander seemed to understand. He did not ask what she felt. He did not ask her to respond. He simply remained close to her.

For a few minutes, the world seemed small. There was no Blackwood Holdings, no succession, no documents, no people watching their every move.
